introduction.situation: Philosophy asks questions about reality, knowledge, meaning, value and inquiry, and has been organised by many schemes.
introduction.complication: Existing groupings mix subject matter with periods, regions, school-level teaching and catch-all headings, so related questions are scattered.
introduction.question: How is everything in philosophy divided by the kind of question it asks?
introduction.answer: Philosophy is divided by what its questions are about: being, knowledge and mind, meaning and inference, value, and the standing of the sciences, mathematics and philosophy itself.

governing_thought: Philosophy is divided by what its questions are about: being, knowledge and mind, meaning and inference, value, and the standing of the sciences, mathematics and philosophy itself.

key_line.rank_note: The pillars run from being, to knowing, to saying, to valuing, to the standing of the sciences and of inquiry itself.

field_check.governing_thought: Philosophy is divided by what its questions are about: being, knowledge and mind, meaning and inference, value, and the standing of the sciences, mathematics and philosophy itself.
key_line: Being is the claim-type concerned with what exists, including fundamental reality, religious questions, action and the place of consciousness in nature.
Knowledge and mind is the claim-type concerned with how we know, what the mind is, and how minds malfunction.
Meaning and inference is the claim-type concerned with valid reasoning and how meaning is produced and understood in language and texts.
Value is the claim-type concerned with what is good, right, beautiful and just, in private life, society and the professions.
The standing of the sciences, mathematics and philosophy is the claim-type concerned with the foundations, methods and history of inquiry, including philosophy's own.
field_check.note: P5 mixes sciences' foundations with history, regional traditions and teaching (not values of subject matter); P1/P2 overlap on consciousness; catch-all and catalogue-style sections; Philosophy for Children scattered.
